findings.title: Native tests assume every SPC secret allocation is locked
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A required native release suite failed on these exact source bytes.
findings.evidence: Exact snapshot source and retained evidence below.
findings.reproduction: Source and standard audit check review.
findings.expected: A best-effort Secret can report unavailable locking. Tests verify secret ownership and properties under explicitly controlled prerequisites.
findings.observed: On exact bd41e4d bytes the native release suite stopped at feistel.rs:320 after is_locked returned false for a newly created Workspace. Other 77 libtest cases passed. Five locations assert locked solely from the target family.
findings.impact: The release suite can reject a valid SPC fallback. The denial cause on the first run was not instrumented. This outcome does not establish an implementation error in the lock backend.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep controlled SPC lock tests. In operation-level tests, check page ownership and any actually required policy or condition the assertion on a verified capability. Avoid replacing the native check with a target-constant expectation.
findings.requiredVerification: Run the complete Linux release suite and a dedicated controlled lock-policy test. Keep first-failure, normal retry and serial receipts distinct.

findings.title: Repository instructions still describe RustSec as covering both lockfiles
findings.evidence: Exact snapshot source and retained evidence below.
findings.reproduction: Source and standard audit check review.
findings.expected: The instructions and audit workflow describe the three active locks.
findings.observed: AGENTS.md describes both locks. CI now audits Cargo.lock, fuzz/Cargo.lock and wasm/Cargo.lock.
findings.impact: A maintainer using the written instructions can overlook an active test and security dependency graph.
findings.recommendedFix: Name all three paths in the workflow summary.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare the instructions to byte-verified workflow and run output.

findings.title: WASM memory documentation overstates physical residue and overflow behavior
findings.evidence: Exact snapshot source and retained evidence below.
findings.reproduction: Source and standard audit check review.
findings.expected: Describe the unzeroized source-level value, actual engine/stack behavior and audited runtime evidence separately.
findings.observed: The text says the extra RSC value lies on the stack and stays there on Wasm. Source establishes an extra Copy value without explicit zeroization. Rustc default stack-first overflow traps, while layouts placing data before the stack can overwrite it.
findings.impact: The documentation assigns a physical location and persistence beyond the retained evidence and oversimplifies target behavior.
findings.recommendedFix: State the copy and missing explicit wipe. Explain the default stack-first trap and alternate layout risk. Scope direct erasure evidence to observed artifacts.
findings.requiredVerification: Review the text against the locked backend and distinguish source observation from optimized runtime memory evidence.

limitations: The first local release suite failed at the Feistel lock assertion. The same compiled Feistel test passed when run alone. The isolated pass does not replace the suite result.

For RSC 0.2.0, source establishes an extra value with no explicit wipe. Neither x86 native stack clearing nor the portable zeroization tests establish retained physical copies on every optimized runtime.

The locked native WorkArea was previously blocked in Miri by the SPC mapping protection mode. Its production cast and allocator path match the tested snapshot. Pure Miri evidence is limited to selected calls.
Android on both targets and iOS device linked in CI. iOS simulator was only linted when exact local evidence is present. None of the mobile paths ran.
The short final-round fuzz campaign used 60 seconds for each of six targets. Full-duration baseline runs with 12232802 cases belong only to 06d7d00.
The retained inline-never CT helper probe uses the locked ctutils and cmov on Linux x86-64, Linux AArch64 and bare Wasm. It does not establish every exact inlined call site or compiler / JIT timing.
The ordinary audit excludes a new full-cost Argon2 corpus replay and release package attestation.

Missing exact Clippy receipts: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu debug, x86_64-apple-darwin debug, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc debug, wasm32-wasip1 debug, wasm32-unknown-unknown release, aarch64-apple-ios-sim debug.
